title: For a changed non-test file whose base overlay passes the whole package, say so in the Base overlays section, so the reviewer sees at once which changed sites have no test

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The reviewer reported this as tool feedback (friction) in ork run ork-20261126-021913-1034, item S617. The `## Base overlays` section gives one `go -C WORKTREE test -overlay ... ./DIR` command per changed non-test Go file. When that file is reverted and the whole package still passes, no test covers the change. The reviewer has to run every command to learn this. In S617 `overlay-1.json` (`handlers.go`) and `overlay-3.json` (`speccheck_state.go`) both passed `./internal/daemon` in full.

The owner decided (adj 618, key `reviewer.overlay-pass-note`, "Run at brief", session 8d711f67, 2026-11-27) that ork runs each overlay's `go test` while it builds the section, bounded and advisory like the vet step, and marks each file whose package passes in full with the file reverted. S623 is folded in: when every changed Go file is a `_test.go` file, the section says a base overlay cannot isolate the change, because the checker and its tests are in the same change.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-27: adj 618 (ork runs each overlay go test at brief time, advisory) and adj 622 (each run gets a 2-minute timeout like vet, sequential; a run past it leaves the entry plain). S623 is merged here.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All new tests are in `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go`, beside `overlayVetHarness` and `overlayVetResult`. Each uses a fake `go` prefix route for `-C W test` with Seq replies and reads real brief output through `baseOverlayReviewer` and `baseOverlayEntries`.
- `TestBaseOverlayMarksPackagePassWithFileReverted`: two changed files a.go and b.go; vet passes both; test exits 0 for a.go and 1 for b.go. Assert the exact a.go command followed by baseOverlayPassNote and the exact plain b.go command. Assert vet/test pairs for overlay-1.json then overlay-2.json, in order.
- `TestBaseOverlayNoPassNoteWhenVetFails`: assert the exact does-not-build entry and no test call when vet fails; include a passing-vet control.
- `TestBaseOverlayPassNoteNeedsAnExitZeroTestRun`: passing control against a nonzero test exit, missing GoBin and a test process reaching its parent deadline. Failed runs keep plain commands, advisory.
- `TestBaseOverlayPassNoteOnNewFile`: a new file maps to the empty replacement and gets the pass note after the new-file marker.
- `TestBaseOverlayTestOnlyChangeSaysOverlayCannotIsolate`: x_test.go plus README.md gets baseOverlayTestOnlyNote once, immediately before the closing paragraph; no Go calls.
- `TestBaseOverlayNoTestOnlyNoteWithProductFile`: test-only control against a.go plus a_test.go and README.md only; neither negative case gets the note.
- `TestBaseOverlayVetsEachOverlayFirst` and `TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherNotOfferedWhenOneFileBuilds`: count only calls whose third argument is vet, since a buildable overlay now also runs go test.
Negative tests include a passing control so each new test fails before implementation.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay.go` add `baseOverlayTestTimeout` next to `baseOverlayVetTimeout`. Its value follows the owner's answer under Owner needed.
2. Add `baseOverlayPassNote = "Passes in full with this file reverted: no test in the package fails for this change, so no test covers it."` and `baseOverlayTestOnlyNote = "Every changed Go file is a test file, so a base overlay cannot isolate the product change: the tests are part of the change. Read each file's base version with `git show` instead."`.
3. Add `(e *Engine) overlayPackagePasses(ctx, rec, overlayFile, pkg string) bool`. It runs `clirun.Run` with `Bin: e.d.goBin()`, `Args: {"-C", rec.Worktree, "test", "-overlay", overlayFile, pkg}` and `Timeout: baseOverlayTestTimeout`. It returns true only when `err == nil` (exit 0). A non-zero exit, a timeout or a failure to start all return false, so the check is advisory like `overlayBuildError`.
4. In the per-file loop of `baseOverlaySection`, after `overlayBuildError` returns "" and the command is built, call `overlayPackagePasses` with `packageArg(p)`. When it is true, write the entry as `line + ": `" + command + "`. " + baseOverlayPassNote`. Otherwise keep the existing entry. Do not run it for the `overlay-all.json` entry, for a file whose vet failed, or for a file whose base could not be read. Entries stay on one line starting "- `".
5. In `baseOverlaySection`, compute `testOnly := len(goFiles) == 0 && hasGoTest`, where `hasGoTest` is true when any path in `changed` ends in `_test.go`. Compute it before the `baseOverlayLimit` truncation. When `testOnly`, write `baseOverlayTestOnlyNote` as its own paragraph just before the closing "The overlays cover non-test Go files only" paragraph.
6. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go` add the new tests and add the vet-only call filter to the two existing tests named under Failing tests.
7. In `docs/design.md` (the `## Base overlays` bullet, 2071-2118) record both: ork runs each buildable overlay's `go test` with the timeout and marks a file whose package passes in full, and a diff whose Go files are all `_test.go` gets the cannot-isolate paragraph. Cite S622, S623 and adj 618. Add the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S622 --text "..."`; do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayMarksPackagePassWithFileReverted ./internal/engine` passes (ok, no FAIL).
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayNoPassNoteWhenVetFails ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayPassNoteNeedsAnExitZeroTestRun ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayPassNoteOnNewFile ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayTestOnlyChangeSaysOverlayCannotIsolate ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayNoTestOnlyNoteWithProductFile ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayVetsEachOverlayFirst ./internal/engine` passes with the vet-only call filter.
- `go test -run TestBaseOverlayAllTogetherNotOfferedWhenOneFileBuilds ./internal/engine` passes with the vet-only call filter.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` prints nothing.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` is green.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In the next reviewer round for a slice that changes a non-test Go file with no test of its own, open the reviewer's brief under the run's role files. In ## Base overlays, that file's entry should end with "Passes in full with this file reverted: ..." after its command. An entry for a file whose revert fails a test should have no such sentence.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In the next reviewer round for a slice whose only Go changes are _test.go files, open the reviewer's brief. ## Base overlays should hold a paragraph saying a base overlay cannot isolate the product change, and no go -C ... test -overlay command.
